title: Auxin Moves Sideways, and the Shoot Bends

scenes.tts: Light an oat seedling from one side, and its shoot bends toward the lamp. The tip is where the light is mainly sensed. But the bend forms lower down. What carries the message between them?
scenes.visual: Lamp at left lights a straight oat seedling; shoot bends toward it; tip and bend zone labelled; a question mark joins them.
scenes.narration: Light an oat seedling from one side, and its shoot bends toward the lamp. The tip is where the light is mainly sensed. But the bend forms lower down. What carries the message between them?

scenes.tts: Charles Darwin and his son Francis lit canary grass seedlings from one side. An opaque cap over the tip greatly reduced bending, even though the lower part was still lit. A transparent glass tube over the tip did not stop it. Light is sensed mainly near the tip, and something passes down to where the bending happens.
scenes.visual: Three seedlings side by side: bare tip bends, opaque cap stays nearly straight, glass tube bends; arrow runs down from the tip.
scenes.narration: Charles Darwin and his son Francis lit canary grass seedlings from one side. An opaque cap over the tip greatly reduced bending, even though the lower part was still lit. A transparent glass tube over the tip did not stop it. Light is sensed mainly near the tip, and something passes down to where the bending happens.

scenes.tts: Peter Boysen-Jensen worked with oat coleoptiles, the sheath over the first leaf of a grass seedling. He cut off tips and set them back in place. The coleoptile still bent below the cut, so the influence crossed a wound. Then he slid mica into a cut below the tip. Dissolved chemicals cannot cross mica. Mica on the lit side left bending intact. Mica on the shaded side blocked it. The signal runs down the shaded side.
scenes.visual: Three coleoptiles lit from the left: cut tip set back still bends; mica on lit side bends; mica on shaded side stays straight; an arrow runs down the shaded side.
scenes.narration: Peter Boysen-Jensen worked with oat coleoptiles, the sheath over the first leaf of a grass seedling. He cut off tips and set them back in place. The coleoptile still bent below the cut, so the influence crossed a wound. Then he slid mica into a cut below the tip. Dissolved chemicals cannot cross mica. Mica on the lit side left bending intact. Mica on the shaded side blocked it. The signal runs down the shaded side.

scenes.tts: Frits Went took the signal out of the plant. He stood cut tips of dark-grown oat coleoptiles on small blocks of agar, then removed the tips. In the dark, he set a block on one side of a decapitated coleoptile. The coleoptile curved away from the block. Plain agar caused no curve. A substance from the tips had entered the agar and sped elongation beneath it. Auxin was identified later, by others.
scenes.visual: Tips stand on an agar block and release a signal into it; the block is set on one side of a decapitated coleoptile, which curves away; a plain agar block leaves it straight.
scenes.narration: Frits Went took the signal out of the plant. He stood cut tips of dark-grown oat coleoptiles on small blocks of agar, then removed the tips. In the dark, he set a block on one side of a decapitated coleoptile. The coleoptile curved away from the block. Plain agar caused no curve. A substance from the tips had entered the agar and sped elongation beneath it. Auxin was identified later, by others.

scenes.tts: Why does the shaded side get more? The Cholodny-Went hypothesis says that light from one side moves auxin sideways, toward the shaded flank. That flank elongates faster, so the shoot bends toward the light. In Arabidopsis hypocotyls, light changes where a carrier called PIN three sits in the cell membrane. PIN carriers sit on one face of a cell, so repositioning them steers auxin.

PIN carriers sit on one face of a cell, so repositioning them steers auxin.
scenes.visual: Shoot block with lit and shaded flanks; auxin blobs move across to the shaded flank, which lengthens, and the shoot bends toward the lamp; a cell with a PIN carrier on one face.

scenes.tts: A worked bioassay shows the logic. These numbers are illustrative, not from a real experiment. A split tip lit from one side gives zero point zero three milligrams per litre of auxin from the lit half, and zero point zero six from the shaded half. A tip kept in the dark gives zero point zero nine, the same total. Light did not destroy auxin on the lit side. It moved auxin to the shaded side. Each flank's growth follows its auxin level, and the curve is the difference.
